title: ddalgak --json output, schema_version 1 (Step 66 engine commands, Step 67 rule commands, Step 75 profile commands)
description: Every document `ddalgak ... --json` prints: the cli-envelope-v1 envelope, the `data` of each command (selected by `command`), and Ddalgak's error codes with their exit codes (docs/CLI_CONTRACT.md §6, docs/DDALGAK_ENGINE.md §6, docs/DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL.md §13). Objects are closed so regression tests notice any change; consumers must still ignore unknown fields and tolerate new enum values (CLI_CONTRACT §8). Privacy is part of the contract: activity entries carry rule IDs and outcome codes only, and no engine or status field ever carries keys, typed text, window titles, paths of other programs or rule content (DDALGAK-SEC-001, DDALGAK-SEC-011). The rule commands show what the user asked for: `rule list` titles, triggers and step types, `rule show` the one requested rule as stored in rules.json, and problem messages name rules, triggers and step fields (never typed text, URLs or arguments).

indicator.description: Step 73 (ADR 0046): what the tray icon, its tooltip and the optional floating badge show. Every state has its own shape and words, never color alone; `ring_struck` marks an engine that is off after an emergency, a lost hook or an unclean exit. `attention` names what needs the user in a code; the floating badge is opt-in (settings.floating_indicator) and drawn by the editor app (Step 74).

ok_enable.description: Step 73: `ddalgak enable|disable`. Without a scope the engine of the running app turns on or off (`scope: engine`, the data of `engine start|stop`; a disable is remembered across restarts). With `--rule`, `--mode` or `--profile` the scope is switched in rules.json through the rule store (the data of a rule write, plus `modes` for a mode and `profile` for a mode or a profile).

ok_release.description: Step 73: `ddalgak release`. The worker releases every key and button in Ddalgak's ledger (`held_by_ddalgak`, released after the answer), the hook forgets its key state, and of the keys Ddalgak could have pressed (`stale.checked`) those Windows still considers pressed and nobody holds get an up (`stale.released`). Counts only, never key names.

mode_state.description: The active mode (Step 72, DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §7.3): the newest held layer or the latched mode, the layers held now, the previous latched mode, the default mode, the precedence chain (the mode and its parents), why and since when. `live: false` when the engine is off or the app is not running: then this is the default mode, where every start begins (the active mode is never restored, ADR 0043). Names and IDs only, never keys.

origin.description: start, rule:<rule id>, released:<rule id> (a held layer's key went up), cli, tray, timeout, one_shot, pause, reload, key_reset

indicator.description: What the tray shows (settings.mode_indicator): off where it is not needed (one mode); the title is always part of the label, never only the color or icon.

allOf.description: Without a live engine, the default mode with nothing held.

active.description: Whether the running engine is in this mode; null without a live engine.

rules.description: Rules the change copied, deleted or took the mode out of.

off_reason.description: Why the engine is off (null while it is on).

origin.description: tray, cli, startup, shutdown, session, emergency, shortcut:<action>, rule:<rule id>

not.description: No rule turns the engine on (DDALGAK-FR-004).

mouse_installed.description: The low-level mouse hook is installed: only while the engine is on and an active rule has a mouse-button trigger (Step 68, ADR 0031).

allOf.description: The keyboard hook exists only while the engine is running or paused (DDALGAK-FR-002).
off_reason is given exactly when the engine is off.

rules.description: The active rules (what the engine runs or will run), counted, plus the saved file and the draft as separate states (Step 67). Without the app, the counts describe the saved file and `active_set`, `in_sync` and `last_reload` are null.

in_sync.description: The active rules equal the saved file (null without the app).

inactive_code.description: Codes of DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §8 that keep a rule inactive: errors, and the *_unsupported infos of this version.

saved_file.description: rules.json as last read. `interrupted_save`: a crash left rules.json.tmp behind; rules.json itself is intact (the next save replaces the temporary file).

active_set.description: The rules the running app holds (the last usable file); null without the app.

profile.description: Step 75: the profile the app runs.

last_reload.description: The last reload that changed something or failed: `applied` (the new file is active) or `kept_previous` (the file is not usable; the previous rules stay active and the code says why).

draft_state.description: An unsaved draft (rules.draft.json) and the saved revision it is based on; stale when the saved rules changed since.

registration.description: registered / taken (RegisterHotKey in the running app); not_running (no app); unavailable (the action had no feature yet: editor.open before Step 74; kept for older apps); unsupported (needs more than RegisterHotKey, e.g. left/right modifiers); wanted (to be registered).

recovered.description: Step 73: after an unclean exit, the keys Ddalgak could have pressed that were checked and those released because Windows still considered them pressed (null after a clean exit).

profile.description: The active profile and its active mode (`mode`; Step 72 adds the full `mode_state`; Step 73 `enabled`: false when the user disabled the profile, then none of its rules run).

allOf.description: Without the app the engine is off for that reason, there is no activity and there are no active rules apart from the saved file; with the app, saved and active rules are compared.

mouse_installed.description: The low-level mouse hook is installed (only while a mouse-button rule is active).

timeout_us.description: Step 73: a callback (or a physical event's wait) this long turns the engine off (`hook_lost`): the user's LowLevelHooksTimeout capped at 1 s, or 300 ms when it is not set; 0 before the first hook.

physical.description: Step 75: key (and, while the mouse hook exists, mouse-button) events from a device, not injected; a count only, no key is kept.

hook_timeouts.description: Step 73: callbacks that reached the hook timeout (each turned the engine off with hook_lost).

source.description: What a rule command read: the saved rules.json or the draft (--draft).

offer.description: A non-destructive resolution in the hotkey contract's style (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §9.5); never applied automatically.

problem.description: One validation finding (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §8). Errors and warnings carry offers, infos none.

app_after_write.description: A running app asked to reload after a saved change: whether the active rules now equal the saved ones. null for dry runs and drafts; `running: false` when no app runs (it reads the file when it starts).

active_profile.description: Step 75: the profile the app runs after the reload (a `profile apply` checks it switched).

ok_test.description: `ddalgak test` (Step 76): `data` is exactly one ddalgak-simulation-v1 document of kind `simulate`, which that schema closes and the CLI's tests validate; only its identifying fields are repeated here.

text_redacted.description: Step 69: the text of each type_text step was replaced by {"redacted": true, "preview": <counts>} (the default; `--show-text` shows it).

targets_redacted.description: Step 70: the launch targets were redacted (the default; `--show-targets` shows them): an open_program path became {"redacted": true, "program": <file name>}, its args {"redacted": true, "count": n}, its working_dir {"redacted": true}, its env {"redacted": true, "names": [...]}, an open_url url {"redacted": true, "shown": <scheme://host/…>}.

rule.description: The rule as stored (ddalgak-rules-v1 `rule`, unknown fields included), with snippet text redacted unless `--show-text` and launch targets redacted unless `--show-targets` was given.

ok.description: No errors (warnings and infos never block).

problems.description: Findings on the rules the change touched (errors there are ones it did not introduce).

anyOf.description: A dry run writes nothing and asks no app.
A draft change leaves the saved and active rules alone.

snapshots.description: Newest first; at most 50 are kept (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §10).

kept.description: rules.json.bak (the replaced version), or rules.corrupt-<time>.json when the replaced file was not usable.

profile_row.description: Step 75: one profile as `profile list` and the editor's profile browser show it. `errors` counts the errors that keep rules of the profile inactive.

rule_line.description: Step 75: a rule in a profile diff or listing: its name, its trigger and the kinds of its steps — never typed text, paths, arguments, environment values or URLs (DDALGAK-SEC-011).

inactive.description: `profile show`: the code that keeps the rule inactive.

profile_diff.description: Step 75: two profiles side by side. `align: trigger` lines up what each trigger does before (left, the active profile) and after (right) a switch; `align: rule_id` lines up two versions of one profile (left: now, right: the version a restore or rollback brings back).

versions.description: Distinct saved versions (history snapshots and save points); 0 for a draft.

switch_preview.description: What a switch to this profile would change; null when it is the active profile.

data.description: Step 75: the rule store's write result; `profiles` are the profiles the change touched, `created` a new profile's ID, `rules` the rules it touched (a duplicate's new rule IDs, a deleted profile's rules).

anyOf.description: A dry run (the preview) writes nothing and asks no app.
A draft change leaves the saved and active rules alone.

data.description: Step 75: `profile apply` changes only active_profile; a running app then switches atomically (runs cancelled, every held key released, the new profile in its default mode). `--dry-run` is the preview.

mode.description: The mode the profile starts in (its default mode).

switched.description: The running app confirmed the switch: it runs this profile and the saved revision. null without an app (it starts with the saved profile) and for a dry run.

anyOf.description: A dry run (the preview) writes nothing and asks no app.
A draft change leaves the saved and active rules alone.

data.description: Step 75: one profile put back as it was in a snapshot or save point, as a new change (itself restorable); the other profiles and the active profile stay.

source.description: The history snapshot or save point the version comes from.

anyOf.description: A dry run (the preview) writes nothing and asks no app.
A draft change leaves the saved and active rules alone.

data.description: Step 75: `profile import` (with --dry-run, the validation preview). The profiles are added NOT active, every rule off and without consent; nothing is opened, typed or run (DDALGAK-SEC-013).

restored_modes.description: Modes the file referred to but did not define (a deleted mode): added empty, so the rules keep their limits.

permissions.description: What the rule needs consent for before it can be turned on; consent is never imported.

targets.description: The exact programs, apps and websites the rule would open: a count unless --show-targets.

missing_programs.description: Program files or working folders that do not exist on this computer.

conflicts.description: An earlier imported rule with the same trigger, modes, conditions and priority, or Ddalgak's own shortcut: they would collide once both are on.

inactive.description: A code that keeps the rule inactive even when turned on (a newer step type, a reserved trigger, …).

anyOf.description: A dry run (the preview) writes nothing and asks no app.
A draft change leaves the saved and active rules alone.

save_point.description: The save point's file name in savepoints/ (null for a dry run, or when nothing was saved yet).

exists.description: false: the profile was deleted; its versions can still be restored.

versions.description: Newest first: every save point, and each history snapshot in which the profile differs from the next older one.

working.description: The profile had no error in that version (a rollback goes only to such versions).

current.description: It equals the profile as saved now.

rollback_to.description: The version `profile rollback` would restore: the newest working one that differs from now.

portable_paths.description: Program and folder paths written under a known-folder token (%LocalAppData%\…).

env_values_removed.description: Environment values of program rules left out (they may be secrets; --include-env-values keeps them).

data.description: Step 75: never the file's content: it is written to `file` (every rule off, no consent, settings or revision).
